content.method: source inspection and installed CLI parser command
findings: CRITICAL: build_command places --sandbox after the resume subcommand (lines 122-133).
codex exec supports --sandbox, but codex exec resume --help does not list it.
codex exec resume --sandbox danger-full-access --help exits 1 with unexpected argument --sandbox; run() maps any nonzero child exit to codex_exec_failed at lines 304-310.
interpretations: The documented promise that the same sandbox selection is applied to new and resumed sessions is not executable with the current CLI argv shape; this directly reproduces the observed resume failure.
limitations: No real resumed agent turn was launched because the parser-level failure is deterministic and launching would widen the read-only audit.

content.method: targeted unittest execution and test-source review
findings: HIGH: resume argv tests assert only list shape or invoke a fake executable, so they never exercise the installed codex resume parser and accept the invalid --sandbox position.

The Intake launcher tests patch subprocess.Popen globally while run() now calls intake.py session-show/session-bind through subprocess.run, producing six mock-related errors plus an integration failure before launcher behavior is exercised.
The agent routing metadata test still expects only Main, Intake, and Workflow references although skills/agents/SKILL.md routes six roles.
Targeted command ran 57 tests and ended with 5 failures and 7 errors; additional stale literal assertions include AI review findings, implementation Work, and decide execution admission.
interpretations: The regression suite is materially out of sync with current launcher and role contracts and cannot protect the resume path.
limitations: pytest is not installed; python3 -m pytest failed and standard unittest was used.

findings: MEDIUM: agents SKILL frontmatter and routing define six roles: Main, Intake, Workflow, Test, Documentation, and Review.
agents/openai.yaml short_description and default_prompt advertise only main and workflow roles.
README correctly says each skill has agents/openai.yaml metadata but does not enumerate the six agents roles.
interpretations: UI metadata understates the callable role surface and can misroute or hide Intake, Test, Documentation, and Review role use.

findings: HIGH: Test Agent contract requires exact commands in the prepared implementation worktree, while specification-direct explicitly has no worktree; test_agent_prompt unconditionally directs every Test Agent to the dedicated worktree.

HIGH: Test Agent contract says a role failure is terminal evidence for following Documentation and Review handoffs, but run_protocol raises turn_failed for a non-completed Test turn and execute immediately returns an error payload, so Documentation and Review Goals are not launched.
interpretations: The Test Agent execution location is undefined/incorrect for specification-direct Work Units, and the implementation short-circuits a documented downstream failure-evidence sequence.
limitations: No live Goal was launched; findings are based on explicit prompt construction and deterministic control flow, supported by existing orchestration tests for the success path only.

content.method: six-role ownership matrix and terminology/order comparison
findings: The core ownership split is otherwise consistent: Main owns Human-facing lifecycle/admission/review/integration; Intake owns bounded evidence; Workflow owns Plan and implementation only; Test owns Human-authorized commands only; Documentation owns affected documents; Review owns static review only.
The implemented success order matches the lifecycle contract: implementation, optional tests or tests-not-run, documentation, review, report material.

LOW: lifecycle.md quotes the launcher prompt as You are the Workflow Agent. You must execute this Work Unit, while implementation says You must execute the named Work Unit; the semantic role boundary is equivalent but the exact quotation is stale.
LOW: execution_prompt accepts resume, but its invalid-mode error says mode must be execution or rework and omits resume.
interpretations: No broad role ownership duplication or missing primary owner was found beyond the Test failure/location conflicts and metadata/test drift.
limitations: Static comparison cannot establish whether every agent obeys prompts at runtime.
